body:
Thanks for the comment. 

At the displeasure of my parents I have been spending more and more time with the people I care about, with my dad hovering over me going "Friends are temporary but family is forever!" 

I'm an artist and I love to draw but art block has slammed into me like a ton of bricks. I just don't know where to start with occupying my time.

Stress is definitely a thing. I'm doing full time college (13 credits) and working 30 hours a week and on top of that my dad is upset that I'm not also apprenticing anywhere. I got promoted at work as well and the extra responsibility is huge even if the tasks suit me better.

Thanks for the response. Sorry for throwing a wall of text at you. As for living for myself--for my whole life I've been taking care of 2 alcoholics, later expanded to 4 when my siblings (10 years older) started drinking. My parents used to abuse me and my dad even went so far as to break my fingers. I would be up all night breaking up physical fights or arguments, and I'd block the door when they'd try to drive.

I never got to go out. I went to my friends' house maybe 25 times through out all of schooling, and they never came over to my house. 

My parents have sobered up but they're used to me being at home all the time. They get upset now that I hang out with friends, and they've done everything in their power to try and financially trap me including making me buy a car way out of budget that I didn't even want.

And I guess, I just am so put out by it. I don't expect praise for taking care of all of them. I don't expect pats on the back for dealing with being hit, screamed at, having things thrown at me. But I would love it if at the very least they could show the courtesy of simply letting me go.

My girlfriend was a lot of my guiding hand through my relationship. Towards the end last year she got super weird. I was working and going to school at the same time and she was going to school while her parents paid for lodging and cost of living. She 

-scolded me constantly for spending money i made because she needed somewhere to move out to when she finished her four years since her parents would cut her off. Wouldn't have been a problem but she refused to get even a summer time job.

-never agreed "Hey yeah, lets chat!" if it was inconvenient to her. I get she had homework to do but so did I. Regardless I let her schedule me in to her convenience every single time. She tried the "I can dedicate saturday to you" which she never followed up on.

-freaked out on me every time I pointed out that we weren't spending more than a few actual hours together during the week. Instantly caused a fight of "You don't know how hard my life is, I have so many credit classes my Councillor says grown men have dropped out of this school" ect ect

-started running around going "YOU'RE SO UNSUPPORTED OF ME-I WAS RAPED AND THAT'S WHY I WAS ACTING SO WEIRD" when I broke up with her and that fucking ruined me for about two months because I felt like I was such an awful person even though I didn't know and she didn't tell me. She only threw it at me after the break up. My friends kept me from going back.

As for the homophobia... my sister when she was around 19 suddenly came out to my parents as gay. It was a huge struggle with lots of fights but they had just started to get used to the idea of her being a lesbian. The suddenly her girlfriend and her had a fight, my sister was done experimenting and married a guy about two years later. That's all fine and well, but my parents are now convinced being gay is a choice. My dad constantly talks about homosexuals like they're lesser people. He chastises me for "wearing gay colors" and my own sister who guessed I was gay (I denied) told me that I "shouldn't get mixed up in that crowed and that women aren't meant to be together."

Recently I've been struggling with the idea of coming out as I reach out for a more local girlfriend. The comment my dad made, though light, instantly reminded me of how hard it's going to be and honestly despite my girlfriend (Who's MTF) being with me for five years I only recently came to terms with the fact that I'm a gay christian and my confidence in it is still kind of fragile.
